editorial.headline: Feed Retail’s Split Decision: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Retailing feed for livestock, poultry, fish and companion animals is nationally open to PMA, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks its PMA registration.
editorial.body:
At its core, this activity is the retail trade in feed for livestock, poultry and fish, alongside food for companion animals. The stated range is concrete: feed rations and concentrates for livestock, poultry and fish, plus bone meal, blood meal and shell meal. It also covers retailing various fish-feed products from public-roadside stalls, the front porch of a shop, or movable and pushable market premises. Those examples include fish feed, fish-feed concentrates and shell meal. The scope is expressly identified as other than direct selling.

The activity is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. This is a scale-wide statement of access to the specified retail activity, not an invitation to blur its boundaries. The record remains focused on defined feed and food products, and on retail settings that include fixed shops as well as the named roadside and market formats. For a founder, the classification begins with that practical distinction: this is a retail activity for animal-feed and companion-animal-food products within the stated scope.

Nationally, it carries open PMA status, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership of the activity. Its stated source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali gives a different result. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today, despite its national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. The Bali record marks the activity as blocked. Its stated reason is that, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope; it is therefore caught by the Bali moratorium recorded on May 13, 2026.

That moratorium is described as island-wide and permanent, applying to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The consequence is unambiguous: national openness does not provide a Bali registration path for this activity. A founder considering this retail scope should treat the national 100% ceiling and Bali’s PMA block as simultaneous facts, rather than competing descriptions of the same rule. The work may be clearly defined, and every scale may be listed as open, yet Bali remains a registration stop for PMA.
